title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Section VII, page 473 of Grothendieck's own numbering, opens a 'Récapitulation sur les épi-glabres'. It sits inside the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes, which follow the Longue Marche. Here S is a base scheme and M a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over S. Equivalently M is a Brauer–Severi P^1-bundle P over S, or locally M = End(F) for a rank-2 vector bundle F. G, SG and PG are the corresponding inner forms of GL2, SL2 and PGL2 over S. For a section rho of M, not necessarily invertible, set v = det rho (reduced norm) and w = Tr rho (reduced trace). Cayley–Hamilton then gives rho^2 - w rho + v = 0. The proposition characterizes 'regular' sections rho. The following conditions are stated to be equivalent: (a) rho is non-scalar in every fibre. (a') A_rho = O_S·1 + O_S·rho is a locally direct-summand, locally free rank-2 submodule of M; by Cayley–Hamilton it is then a commutative sub-algebra, locally free of rank 2. (b) Locally for the Zariski topology there is a cyclic vector e0, meaning (e0, rho e0) is a basis of F. (b') There is a line subbundle D0 with F = D0 + rho(D0). (b'') F, viewed as an O_S[T]-module with T acting by rho, is locally monogenic. (c) F_rho is isomorphic to O_S[T]/(T^2 - wT + v). (c') Locally rho has companion-matrix form [[0,-v],[1,w]], continued on the next page together with the transposed form (c''). (d)/(d') The commutant of rho is exactly O_S[rho], universally under base change, respectively fibrewise. The next page gives the proofs: (a)⇔(a') via direct summands of O_S·1; (a)⇒(b) by choosing a non-eigenvector in the fibre and lifting it; equivalence with the companion form; reduction of (b)⇒(d) to fields after base change. Purpose: a recapitulation setting up the regular sections of these twisted GL2s. These are presumably used afterwards to analyse 'épi-glabre' elements and their commutant tori (A_rho is a rank-2 étale-or-not algebra, i.e. a possibly degenerate maximal torus of G). This feeds the study of the braid/loop relations in PGL2-forms from the preceding pages, which reduce conditions like det(sigma+rho) = 0 to Tr(sigma rho) = 2.
errors: Next page, parenthetical: 'rho e1 = -v rho e0 - w e0' is a slip. It should read rho e1 = rho^2 e0 = -v e0 + w e1, which is consistent with the matrix [[0,-v],[1,w]] that is written correctly.

Minor gap: (b)⇒(a) and the base-change stability in (d) are only sketched. They are true: on a field, a non-scalar 2x2 matrix has commutant k[rho], and since O_S[rho] is locally free of rank 2 as a direct summand, the commutant, being the kernel of ad(rho), has constant fibre rank 2 and therefore commutes with base change.

ideas.what: Regular sections of a rank-4 Azumaya algebra: equivalence of non-scalar on fibres, existence of a cyclic vector, monogenic module structure, companion-matrix normal form, and commutant equal to O_S[rho] universally
ideas.modern_name: Regular elements / regular centralizers in (inner forms of) GL2 over a base; cyclic vectors; companion matrices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical linear algebra (Frobenius); regular elements over general bases: Kostant, Steinberg (1960s); SGA3 for maximal tori in reductive group schemes
ideas.where_published: Related material on regular elements and Cartan subgroups appears in SGA3, Exp. XIII–XIV, but not in this explicit rank-2 Azumaya formulation as far as known

ideas.what: A_rho = O_S + O_S rho as a rank-2 commutative subalgebra of M determined by Cayley–Hamilton, i.e. the commutant torus of a regular element
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic subalgebra / maximal commutative subalgebra of a quaternion (Azumaya) algebra; centralizer torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (quaternion algebras); Knus et al., The Book of Involutions, for the general base case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine recapitulation of standard facts about regular elements in rank-2 matrix and Azumaya algebras over a base. The only mildly interesting item is the coined term 'épi-glabre', whose meaning would be established later in the notes; nothing on this page is new mathematics.
